---
title: "Templates"
description: "A template decides how every slide looks: layouts, colors, fonts, logos and pictures."
---

This page covers what a template is, the six templates that come with
banners, and the options that a template of your own can set.

## One line changes the whole deck

A template draws every slide of the deck. The slides only hold their content
(titles, text, plots); the template decides where each piece goes and which
colors and fonts it uses. That is why one call changes the look of a whole
presentation:

```python
from banners import EXECUTIVE, configure

configure(template=EXECUTIVE)
```

Every slide created after this call uses `EXECUTIVE`. Without a call to
`configure(template=...)`, banners uses `Template()`, the default template.

All of them are importable from `banners`:

```python
from banners import COSMOS, EXECUTIVE, INSTITUTIONAL, TERRA, VIBRANT, Template
```

## What a template is made of

A `Template` combines three things:

- **Layouts**: where the title, the content, the logo and the bottom bar go on
  each kind of slide. They are built into banners; the
  [Layouts](layouts.qmd) page shows how a slide picks one.
- **A `Palette`**: the colors, by role (title, text, background, bar…). See
  [Palettes](palettes.qmd).
- **A `Theme`**: fonts, title weight, icon stroke and a size multiplier. See
  [Themes](themes.qmd).

On top of those, a template can carry logos, pictures and a few switches:

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `logo_on_dark`, `logo_on_light` | Logo drawn on dark slides (cover, closing) and on light ones. A URL, a file path or raw bytes. |
| `mark` | Small symbol in the top-right corner of content slides: an image or an icon name such as `"chart"`. |
| `cover_image`, `divider_image` | Photo used by every cover, or every divider, unless the slide sets its own. |
| `divider_icon` | Large icon on dividers without a photo. |
| `closing_image` | Picture next to the closing title. |
| `bar`, `bar_split` | Draw the two-color bar along the bottom edge, and how much of it is the primary color. |
| `auto_contrast` | Replace a title color that would be hard to read on its background. Turn it off to keep exact brand colors. |

Images given as URLs are loaded by the browser when the slide is shown;
paths and bytes are embedded in the slide.

## A template of your own

A template is a plain Python object, so a deck can define its own in a
notebook cell and use it with `configure()`:

```python
from banners import Palette, Template, Theme, configure

ours = Template(
    palette=Palette(primary="#0f766e", secondary="#f59e0b"),
    theme=Theme(heading_font="Georgia, serif"),
    mark="chart",
)
configure(template=ours, team="Data Office", date="2026")
```

[Your organization's template](../howto/organization-template.qmd) builds a
complete one, with logos.

## Changing only the colors or the fonts

To keep a template's layouts and change only its colors or fonts, pass a
palette or a theme to `configure()` instead of building a new template:

```python
from banners import BLUE, COSMOS, configure

configure(template=COSMOS, palette=BLUE)
```

The palette given to `configure()` replaces the template's palette as a whole.
The next pages explain palettes and themes in detail.
